title: Local Minimax Confidence Interval Length for Transported Survival Contrasts under Modifier Misspecification
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 7 < 7.4; salvageable=false within scope.
gap_reasons: The matched lower bound and attainment concern the specified finite-cell survival likelihood under bounded Fisher-local departures; they do not establish robustness to nonlocal modifier failure or a general survival-model frontier.

The methodological contribution is a connected-action refinement of [Evans–Hansen–Stark duality](https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~stark/Preprints/617.pdf), and [Armstrong–Kline–Sun](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3982/ECTA21991) already permits nonlinear fixed-length centers.
The stronger comparison establishes a strict separation at one coefficient/radius witness, without characterizing gains across regimes.
The total attaining procedure uses rational enumeration and a slow diagonal schedule, with no demonstrated computationally practical implementation or finite-sample performance.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established the finite-model Gaussian reduction, strong duality, original-data local lower bound, uniform attainment, certified finite brackets, and a witness-specific gap against randomized nonlinear fixed-length intervals. D0.5 passed mathematical and cited-source review, but graded the delivered package subfield below the required field floor. The general connectedness frontier and extensions beyond the local finite-cell model remain open; no Lean formalization began.
tldr: The paper gives the sharp local minimax worst expected length of randomized connected \(90\%\) confidence intervals for a transported time-two survival treatment contrast when a prespecified modifier reduction can fail within a bounded Fisher-normal \(n^{-1/2}\) radius. The observed censored likelihood yields two independent Gaussian channels. Connected-action strong duality, a matching original-data local lower bound, and a total data-only attaining interval identify the exact decision value uniformly on compact interior base sets through zero modifier sensitivity. Finite primal and connected-dual computations converge to that value. The specified censored covariate-shift witness has the certified bracket \([4.8625,4.8636]\), and a separate endpoint-prior oracle certificate proves \(V_1\le4.8636<4.87<W_{\mathrm{fix}}(1)\) against every randomized nonlinear connected interval of deterministic constant length. Connected and arbitrary-set values agree when \(\kappa H\le\sigma\); the complete connectedness frontier and an optimized strict-value region remain open.
gap: Existing survival-transport theory treats the modifier subset as valid, bounded-misspecification work emphasizes point estimation or fixed-length calibration, and expected-measure confidence-set theory permits unrestricted set actions. The carried source audit identifies no theorem that identifies the connected-interval value, proves the same-experiment survival lower bound, or supplies a plug-in attaining rule at vanishing modifier sensitivity.
fill: An explicit randomized-source identification bridge and a compatible full-data lift connect the causal target to the observed likelihood. The project proves connected strong duality and optimizer existence, gives convergent certified primal--dual brackets, establishes the original-data local asymptotic minimax converse on explicit triangular likelihood neighborhoods, and constructs a data-only interval uniformly honest on compact interior base sets attaining the value.
